card.title: IPhone Panic Bitmask (13 and up)

claims.statement: From iPhone 13 on, SMC panic sensor values are bitmasks: each bit is one sensor, and combinations produce new values (e.g. on iPhone 14, 0x400000 wireless flex + 0x200000 prox = 0x600000).
iPhone 13–15 report the value in hexadecimal; iPhone 16 reports it in decimal; iPhone 12 and older report sensor names (e.g. mic1).
Decoding the value into individual bits (e.g. via a hex-to-binary converter) shows which sensors are flagged.

procedure: Convert the reported value to binary.
Map each set bit to the model's sensor list.
Treat undocumented combinations as multiple simultaneous faults.
card.caveats: The source page itself says its codes need verification and lists wrong decimal values (0x400000 is 4194304, 0x200000 is 2097152, 0x600000 is 6291456); corrected here. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
